title: Skate Park Design Consultation
subtitle: A community engagement report prepared by [Group 2] for [Council 1], delivered through the VCNITY platform.
purpose: This report presents findings from a commissioned community engagement on the proposed redesign of a local skate park. The commissioning body required feedback from young people aged 12–25 on safety, accessibility, and design preferences. All findings are de-identified and were reviewed by the group's facilitator before submission. No raw recordings, photographs, or identifying information are included.
findingsIntro: Each finding below follows the commissioned report structure: commissioning body, research question, method, analysis approach, and deliverable status. AI confidence is noted where a finding was flagged. The facilitator resolved all flags before this report was released.

findings.title: Safety and accessibility of the skate area
findings.deliveredBy: [Group 2], on behalf of its members, facilitated by VCNITY
findings.researchQuestion: What do young people aged 12–25 need from the proposed skate park redesign, and what barriers currently affect their safe and accessible use of the space?
findings.method: Three-method engagement running 12–26 August 2026: an in-person drop-in session (Thursday afternoon, 14 sticky-note wall photos captured), facilitator-led individual interviews (audio transcribed, 3 participants), and an online survey (61 responses, multiple choice and free text). Total participants: 47.
findings.analysis: Thematic coding applied to qualitative responses; survey data aggregated with frequency counts. AI flagged one quote for potential identification — facilitator reviewed and paraphrased before submission.

sources.quote: The ramp near the entrance has a crack that I've tripped on twice. It needs fixing before anything else.
sources.whyItMatters: Physical safety hazards were the single most cited barrier to park use. This quote captures a direct, recurring structural risk mentioned across 37 of 47 participants. It directly supports the finding’s recommendation for infrastructure audit as the first priority.

sources.quote: Lighting is really bad at night — feels unsafe after 6pm, especially in winter.
sources.whyItMatters: Lighting concerns were consistently linked to evening and winter use, pointing to a distinct safety gap from the entrance-ramp issue above. Supports a secondary recommendation on lighting upgrades.

sources.quote: [Paraphrased by facilitator] Participant described feeling excluded from the main bowl area due to skill level and perceived social dynamics.
sources.whyItMatters: Social-inclusion barriers were harder to surface than physical ones and only emerged through interview, not survey, responses. AI flagged the original quote as potentially identifying; the facilitator paraphrased it before inclusion.

sources.quote: "No helmet rack" — written by participant during drop-in session.
sources.whyItMatters: A small but recurring amenity gap raised independently across multiple sticky notes. Included as a low-cost, high-visibility fix alongside the larger infrastructure recommendations.

sources.quote: Wheelchair access at the side gate is blocked by a permanent barrier. Nobody seems to know who put it there.
sources.whyItMatters: A smaller group raised this, but it describes an outright access barrier rather than a preference, which is why it is retained as a distinct accessibility finding rather than folded into the general safety theme.

findings.title: Design preferences and feature priorities
findings.deliveredBy: [Group 2], on behalf of its members, facilitated by VCNITY
findings.researchQuestion: Which design features (ramps, rails, bowls, lighting, seating) matter most to prospective users, and how should limited budget be prioritised?
findings.method: Survey ranking question (61 responses) plus drop-in session sticky-note votes (14 photographed boards).
findings.analysis: Frequency-ranked feature list cross-checked against drop-in votes; no identification flags raised.

findings.title: Inclusivity and representation gaps
findings.deliveredBy: [Group 2], on behalf of its members, facilitated by VCNITY
findings.researchQuestion: Which groups of young people are under-represented in this engagement, and what would improve access for them?
findings.method: Cross-tabulation of survey respondent demographics against the local youth population profile; interview notes reviewed for access barriers raised.
findings.analysis: Gap identified for younger (12–14) and female respondents; one interview quote flagged for potential identification and paraphrased by the facilitator before inclusion.
